default: This function performs real local computation and should be tested
in the normal R sense: call the function with realistic arguments
and assert on its actual return value, not a mock.
client_existing_setup: This function works on DataSHIELD connections (client side). The
package's test setup and helper files (shown further below) already
establish a DSLite connection. Use exactly the connection object, data
symbol, tables and helper functions they define, under the names they
use — do NOT write your own login/connection code, and do NOT assume
data beyond what those files assign. Leave dslite_dataset empty — it
is not used when reusing an existing setup.

intro: This function works on DataSHIELD connections (client side) and is
tested against DSLite (an in-process, serverless implementation of
the DataSHIELD server interface) — real execution and real
assertions, not mocking. No DSLite test setup exists yet for this
package, so one will be generated using one of DSLite's built-in
canned datasets. Pick the single best-fitting option and return its
name as dslite_dataset (exactly as written below, e.g. "CNSIM"):
outro: The generated setup file logs in and defines `conns` (the DSLite
connections to pass as `datasources`), with the chosen dataset
already assigned on every study under the symbol `D` — so refer to
it as "D" (and its columns as e.g. "D$LAB_TSC"), and do NOT write
your own login/connection code. Server-side methods are registered

utility_local: This function is part of a DataSHIELD UTILITY package (analyst side)
and does not use DataSHIELD connections: it works on local files,
folders, projects or packages. Test it for real, not with mocks of the
function itself: run it inside a temporary directory
(withr::local_tempdir(), or the package's own temp paths from its
setup/helper files) and never touch the user's home or working
directory. Assert on the return value and on the files and folders it
creates and their content. Replace only calls that would install
packages, reach the network or open an RStudio project/session, with
packages, e.g. renv or usethis). Use the objects and settings the
package's setup/helper files define. Leave dslite_dataset empty.
